definitions.explanation: lasting only a short time; easily lost or destroyed; having a fragile, impermanent quality

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}は{儚|はかな}い。
{桜|さくら}の{美|うつく}しさは{儚|はかな}いからこそ{愛|あい}される。
examples.english: Cherry blossoms are loved precisely because their beauty is fleeting.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{儚|はかな}い{笑顔|えがお}が{印象|いんしょう}に{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Her fragile smile left an impression on me.

notes:
{儚|はかな}い expresses the transient, ephemeral nature of things, often with a sense of beauty or sadness.

FORMS:
- Attributive: {儚|はかな}い + noun
- Predicate: {儚|はかな}い
- Adverbial: {儚|はかな}く
- Noun form: {儚|はかな}さ (transience)

KANJI NOTE:
- The kanji {儚|はかな} ({人|にんべん} + {夢|ゆめ}) literally suggests "person + dream," evoking the dreamlike, insubstantial quality of fleeting things.
- Often written in hiragana (はかない) in modern usage.

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
- Central to Japanese aesthetics ({物|もの}の{哀|あわ}れ)
- Associated with cherry blossoms, fireflies, and other symbols of transience
- Reflects Buddhist concepts of impermanence ({無常|むじょう})

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {儚|はかな}い{命|いのち} (fleeting life)
- {儚|はかな}い{夢|ゆめ} (ephemeral dream)
- {儚|はかな}い{美|うつく}しさ (transient beauty)
- {儚|はかな}い{希望|きぼう} (fragile hope)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {短|みじか}い (short - neutral, objective)
- {束|つか}の{間|ま} (momentary - time-focused)
- {脆|もろ}い (fragile - physical fragility)

REGISTER: Literary/formal. Often used in poetry and emotional contexts.
